summary: All five blocking findings expose unresolved compatibility or executable CI contracts and require bounded spec repairs.

items.title: Duplicate selector rule conflicts with file-spec union
items.rationale: Strictness must distinguish mutually exclusive single-valued suite selectors from the existing multi-valued file selector union.
items.evidence: tests/run.js accumulates repeated --file, --pattern, and positional inputs, while --preset, --scope, --agent, and --all select one directory mode.

items.title: `--list --json` lacks an output contract
items.rationale: Parseability alone cannot prove discovery; a minimal versioned selection and category/file listing contract is required for implementation and tests.
items.evidence: The current runner has category grouping and discovered files but no listing mode or machine-readable shape.

items.title: `test:ci` targets are not concretely identifiable
items.rationale: Credential-free coverage needs exact commands/files and a schema-aware acceptance stub rather than the flow-gate-only fixed response helper.
items.evidence: tests/helpers/stub-agent.js emits one fixed JSON response, while docs enrich/text and quality verification require different schema-shaped responses.

items.title: Zero-target acceptance failure has no runner owner
items.rationale: Discovery should remain side-effect-free in targets.js and tests/acceptance/run.js must own non-zero process behavior for empty or unknown target resolution.
items.evidence: package.json invokes tests/acceptance/run.js, which already owns argument validation and child test execution.

items.title: `test:agent` preservation omits its current consumer
items.rationale: The retained real-provider command cannot be verified until report.test.js imports the actual acceptance helpers and selects the discovered base fixture.
items.evidence: tests/agent/report.test.js imports ../../acceptance from tests/agent and requests node, while the repository contains only the base acceptance fixture/test pair.
